Bumblebee: Keep the natural small head connected and fully exposed in profile. Show real chewing jaw edges below the eye without enlarging them, and offset all six legs with visible roots. Wings remain small; no pink fill in wings or fur.
Butterfly: Keep the slender body and actual coiled proboscis. Do NOT invent biting jaws to satisfy a mandible label. Offset the three near and three far legs naturally, especially the front tarsi; preserve separate clubbed antennae.
Cave Cricket: Wingless anatomy is mandatory, no membrane wings. Paint the entire animal and every long antenna much smaller inside the central 650px box; both full natural antenna tips must remain inside the 275px margin. Expose real mouth edges and separated front feet.
Cricket: Include full natural long antennae with wide margins by painting the whole cricket smaller. Keep both antenna roots and tips distinct and show the small actual head and chewing jaws. No enlarged artificial mandibles.
Damselfly: Keep naturally short bristle antennae, separate side-set eyes, and extremely slender abdomen. Fold wings along the back with clean pale neutral opaque paint in membrane surfaces, no pink key contamination. Spread six real legs so their roots and feet read.
Diving Beetle: Separate the far front leg from the near front leg, keeping its upper joint, lower shin and tarsus continuously visible beneath the head and thorax. Keep natural oar hind legs and yellow-rimmed oval body.
Dobsonfly: Offset all six legs so the middle and front tarsi and far front upper joint remain readable. Both thin antennae should be fully painted and naturally attached without overlap; keep authentic male sickle jaws.
Dragonfly: Retain four naturally spread wings, no beetle wing covers. Use pale neutral opaque wing membrane paint with clear veins, no pink background blended inside. Make six legs distinguishable below the thorax without thickening or inventing segments.
Fly: Every leg must connect continuously to its thoracic root. No floating far front foot. Offset far hind leg to expose the complete lower segment. Keep real sponging mouthparts, never invent chewing mandibles.
Giant Water Bug: Expose small actual piercing rostrum beneath the head, paired hooked forelegs and separated middle/hind legs. Keep naturally small tucked antennae and leaf-shaped body, not a generic beetle.
Grasshopper: Offset far hind thigh and far front lower leg so those real segments remain distinguishable. Maintain short antennae and natural jumping proportions; keep the six thoracic leg attachments.
Honeybee: Show the natural head contour and actual small chewing jaw edges; do not enlarge them. Offset all six legs with clean roots. Keep neutral pale wings without pink in membranes or fur.
Leafcutter Ant: Keep the canonical leaf fragment small and visibly gripped at its true mouth attachment. Expose the far front leg knee and tarsus, and keep thoracic spines true to species without enlarging them.
Mantis: Show real small jaws below the triangular head and the complete near middle leg including tarsus. Keep long prothorax and folded raptorial forelegs without doubling or crossing appendages.
Mayfly: Face RIGHT with head clearly at right. Keep adult tiny reduced mouthparts, no invented chewing mandibles. Upright wings and long rear filaments stay authentic; separate six legs and short antennae without thickening them.
Mosquito: Retain natural slender legs and piercing proboscis, not chewing jaws. Keep all six leg roots and endpoints separate, preserve two wings and small head without enlarging them to resemble a beetle.
Orchid Bee: Separate the near middle knee and far middle lower leg from tongue and other legs. Keep the long natural tongue trailing beneath with visible space, metallic body and swollen hind tibia.
Scorpionfly: Both antennae must be continuously painted from head to natural fine tip, separated from wings and background, without thickening to fake reference anatomy. Keep the male curled genital bulb and authentic beak.
Stick Insect: Keep the twig-thin wingless body and natural leg lengths. Separate near and far knees and feet clearly in a grounded stance; do not add wings, enlarged jaws or a bulky beetle body.
Stonefly: Expose complete far front and rear leg joints below the thorax, both antenna roots and fine tips, plus actual small mouth edges. Retain flat folded wings and two cerci.
Water Strider: Clearly separate exactly six thoracic legs and two antennae. Keep small boat body with natural long middle and hind legs, never add spider legs or thicken joints to imitate a beetle.
Bee: Offset near middle tarsus and expose real head/chewing mouth contours. Keep fine fur grouped with crisp edges and wing membranes pale neutral, without any pink contamination.
Ladybug: Show the complete far hind lower leg and tiny real mouthparts below tucked head. Keep domed spotted red wing cases; do not enlarge the head or invent large jaws.
Locust: Separate near front upper leg from neck/chest silhouette so the natural knee and attachment are visible. Retain short antennae and authentic large jumping hind legs.
Water Beetle: Separate near front upper leg and knee from the head and thorax with a clear natural gap. Keep short clubbed antennae and flattened fringed oar hind legs; no pink fringe.
Cassowary: Keep casque, wattles and black hairlike plumage compact and continuously attached, no wispy isolated strands. Natural upright neck and two powerful legs remain; do not add wings or tail.
Eagle: Keep compact continuous feather groups at the belly and leg roots; reveal the natural upper leg transition and strong talons without stray feather islands. Preserve booted legs, brow and hooked beak.
Godwit: Expose the far thigh transition below the flank by offsetting the two legs in a natural standing pose. Keep long slim dark legs, long slightly upturned bill and cinnamon barred breast.
Grebe: Feet must have separate individually LOBED toes, never continuous duck-like webs. Keep rounded tailless rear and natural short rear-positioned legs. Compact continuous crest and cheek ruff, no loose fragments.
Guillemot: Keep upright chocolate-and-white shape with compact continuous neck/chest contour, short authentic tail and short naturally attached legs. No stray neck or belly islands.
